items.title: Can you believe it? An investigation into the impact of retraction source credibility on the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments, we found that source trustworthiness but not source expertise indeed influences retraction effectiveness
judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect refers to the finding that people often continue to rely on misinformation in their reasoning even if the information has been retracted.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada com dois experimentos sobre retratação, usando cenários neutros (sem indicação de política, saúde ou COVID-19). O achado extraído reflete fielmente o resumo: a confiabilidade da fonte importa, e a influência continuada persiste mesmo com retratações críveis. O método descrito combina com o resumo.

items.title: Exploring factors that mitigate the continued influence of misinformation

judge.evidence_empirical: Across three studies, we evaluated the relative contribution of three factors (i.e., targeting the misinformation, providing an alternative explanation, and relative importance of the misinformation content) to the reduction of the CIE.
judge.evidence_topic: The term “continued influence effect” (CIE) refers to the phenomenon that discredited and obsolete information continues to affect behavior and beliefs.
judge.reason: O achado extraído é suportado pelo resumo: "we found that alternative provision consistently resulted in CIE reduction".

items.title: The role of discomfort in the continued influence effect of misinformation

judge.evidence_empirical: Studies 1 and 2 found that retractions of misinformation elicit psychological discomfort, and this discomfort predicts continued belief in and use of misinformation.
judge.evidence_topic: Research examining the continued influence effect (CIE) of misinformation
judge.reason: O resumo não especifica a natureza dos materiais ou do cenário utilizados, portanto não é possível verificar se são neutros (fictícios, sem conotação política ou de saúde), condição exigida pelo recorte do pesquisador. Os demais critérios são atendidos: o estudo é empírico, o método descrito está alinhado com o resumo, e o achado principal está sustentado.

items.title: The independent effects of source expertise and trustworthiness on retraction believability: The moderating role of vested interest

judge.evidence_empirical: Study 1 demonstrated that... Study 2 found similar effects...
judge.evidence_topic: lead to less continued belief in misinformation
judge.reason: The article reports experiments on the effect of retractions on continued belief in misinformation, matching the request’s focus. The materials appear neutral (abstract does not indicate political/health topics), the study is empirical, the extracted method aligns with the abstract, and the finding is supported by the abstract.

items.title: Comparing the use of open and closed questions for Web-based measures of the continued-influence effect

judge.evidence_empirical: We implemented this basic procedure online (Exp. 1A, n = 78), comparing standard open-ended responses to an alternative procedure using closed-ended responses (Exp. 1B, n = 75). Finally, we replicated these findings in a larger preregistered study (Exps. 2A and 2B, n = 323).
judge.evidence_topic: using the continued-influence effect (CIE), in which participants read a series of statements about an unfolding event, one of which is unambiguously corrected later.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) com experimentos online usando uma história fictícia sobre um evento, e mede referências à desinformação após correção. Portanto, está no tópico e é empírico. O método descrito confere com o resumo, e o achado principal tem suporte literal no resumo.

items.title: Does explaining the origins of misinformation improve the effectiveness of a given correction?

judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments, we examined whether a correction that explained misinformation as originating either from intentional deception or an unintentional error was more effective than a correction that only identified the misinformation as false.
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation often has a continuing influence on event-related reasoning even when it is clearly and credibly corrected; this is referred to as the continued influence effect. The present work investigated whether a correction’s effectiveness can be improved by explaining the origins of misinformation.
judge.reason: Abstract clearly describes experiments on the continued influence effect with neutral scenarios; finding about explanation not improving correction effectiveness is directly stated.

items.title: Examining the role of information integration in the continued influence effect using an event segmentation approach

judge.evidence_empirical: Experiments 1 and 2 employed spatial event segmentation boundaries in an attempt to manipulate the ease with which a retraction can be integrated into a participant's mental event model.
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation regarding the cause of an event often continues to influence an individual's event-related reasoning, even after they have received a retraction. This is known as the continued influence effect (CIE).
judge.reason: O achado extraído ('Experimento 2 reduziu o CIE; Experimento 1 sem efeito') é diretamente sustentado pelo resumo: 'Experiment 1 showed no impact of an event boundary, Experiment 2 yielded evidence that an event boundary resulted in a reduced CIE.'

items.title: Listening to Misinformation while Driving: Cognitive Load and the Effectiveness of (Repeated) Corrections

judge.evidence_empirical: Participants listened to corrections that repeated misinformation while in a driving simulator.
judge.evidence_topic: Corrected misinformation can continue to influence inferential reasoning.
judge.reason: The abstract explicitly addresses the continued influence effect of corrected misinformation and describes an experiment with a driving simulator, neutral materials, and the finding matches the extracted statement.

items.title: Executive function and the continued influence of misinformation: A latent-variable analysis

judge.evidence_empirical: Participants completed several measures of EF subcomponents, including those of updating and inhibition, as well as set shifting, and a standard CIE task.
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation can continue to influence reasoning after correction; this is known as the continued influence effect (CIE).
judge.reason: O artigo trata explicitamente do efeito de influência continuada (CIE) com experimento em humanos, materiais neutros (tarefa CIE padrão), análise de dados próprios. O método extraído coincide com o descrito no resumo. O achado principal é diretamente respaldado pelo resultado do resumo.

items.title: Did he or didn't he? Mixed evidence for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions

judge.evidence_empirical: "Here we report three experiments that tested for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions using a non-dynamic impression-formation task... Participants formed an impression of a fictitious person based on a series of behaviour statements."
judge.evidence_topic: "Here we report three experiments that tested for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions using a non-dynamic impression-formation task... Participants formed an impression of a fictitious person based on a series of behaviour statements."
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada da informação falsa retratada, com cenários fictícios neutros e três experimentos com participantes humanos. O método e achado extraídos conferem com o resumo.

items.title: Does Mud Really Stick? No Evidence for Continued Influence of Misinformation on Newly Formed Person Impressions

judge.evidence_empirical: Across four experiments, we investigated the impact of person-related misinformation and its correction on dynamic (moment-to-moment) impression formation.
judge.evidence_topic: Despite robust evidence that misinformation continues to influence event-related reasoning after a clear retraction, evidence for the continued influence of misinformation on person impressions is mixed.
judge.reason: O resumo afirma que, em cada experimento, os participantes desconsideraram completamente a desinformação após a retratação e que não houve evidência de influência continuada sobre impressões de pessoas, o que sustenta integralmente o achado extraído.

items.title: The inhibitory impact of collaboration on the continued influence effect of misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect (CIE) of misinformation refers to the persistence of misinformation's impact on memory and inference even when individuals are aware of a retraction.
judge.reason: O artigo trata do efeito de influência continuada (CIE) com experimentos usando cenários fictícios, sem conotação política ou de saúde. Os métodos descritos no resumo batem com os dados extraídos e o achado principal é integralmente sustentado pelo texto do resumo.

items.title: Relative source credibility affects the continued influence effect: Evidence of rationality in the CIE

judge.evidence_empirical: "In two experiments ( N = 151, N = 146), informant credibility and retractor credibility were independently manipulated."
judge.evidence_topic: "The Continued Influence Effect (CIE) is the phenomenon that retracted information often continues to influence judgments and inferences." e "Participants read a fictitious news report..."
judge.reason: O artigo atende a todos os critérios do pedido: trata do efeito de influência continuada da informação falsa (CIE), usa cenários fictícios neutros, relata dois experimentos com participantes humanos medindo julgamentos após retratação. O método e o tipo de estudo extraídos condizem com o resumo. O achado extraído é sustentado literalmente pelo resumo.

items.title: Combating false information in military situations: Striking the right balance between continued influence effect and overcorrection

judge.evidence_empirical: A total of 61 participants read four military scenarios designed to simulate decision‐making, followed by an assessment of their inferential reasoning.
judge.evidence_topic: the continued influence effect (CIE), where attitudes persist in alignment with FI. This research aimed to examine the effect of an FI correction within military scenarios.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) após correção de informação falsa, usando cenários militares fictícios (materiais neutros). É um experimento com participantes humanos medindo raciocínio inferencial, conforme exigido. O método extraído coincide com o resumo, e o achado de ausência de CIE e presença de supercorreção é diretamente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Failure to accept retractions: A contribution to the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_empirical: The current study explored whether this effect reflects, at least in part, an unwillingness of some readers to accept changes to their understanding. Experiment 1 assessed this using a continued influence effect paradigm... Experiment 2 included... Experiment 3 modified...
judge.evidence_topic: Previous research has shown that when information about a narrative event is retracted, people continue to use that information even though it has been explicitly identified as incorrect.
judge.reason: O resumo aborda o efeito de influência continuada com cenários narrativos neutros (sem menção a política, vacinas ou COVID-19), utilizando experimentos com participantes humanos. O método extraído corresponde exatamente aos experimentos descritos. O achado principal é sustentado pelo trecho: 'Overall, these findings suggest that at least some of the evidence for the continued use of retracted information may be due to some people not accepting the retraction.'

items.title: I know It's false, but I keep thinking as if it were true: A replication study of Johnson and Seifert's (1994) continued influence effect

judge.evidence_empirical: The present research investigated the direct replicability of their study with a French-speaking sample, comparing the inferences drawn by an FI group (n = 21) to those made by a control group (n = 23).
judge.evidence_topic: False Information (FI) is a critical societal issue, made even more pressing by our inability to mitigate its influence through correction. Researchers Johnson and Seifert (1994, Experiment 1A) penned a seminal paper on this "Continued Influence Effect" (CIE) ...
judge.reason: O artigo é um experimento com participantes humanos que investiga diretamente o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) após correção, usando materiais neutros (replicação do estudo clássico de Johnson & Seifert, que emprega cenário fictício). Ele coleta dados próprios, e o método e achado extraídos coincidem com o resumo.
